ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 2 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — John Henry Holliday — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: Two-week follow-up on treatment with infectious diseases consultation

text.paragraph: Two-week follow-up on tuberculosis treatment, seen the same day by infectious diseases. [S]

Mr. Holliday is a 21-year-old dentist with cavitary pulmonary tuberculosis who returns two weeks after diagnosis and is seen by infectious diseases today. He started isoniazid, rifampin, pyrazinamide, ethambutol, and pyridoxine two days after the first visit, once the nucleic acid amplification test confirmed tuberculosis, and has taken all thirteen doses on daily video calls with the health department nurse. His cough is less frequent, the blood streaks in his sputum have stopped, and the night sweats are lighter. He has mild nausea in the hour after the morning doses, eased by taking them at bedtime with a small snack. His urine and tears are orange, as he was warned. He has no yellowing, dark urine, abdominal pain, rash, numbness, or change in vision or color. He is isolating at home and not working; his roommate is being tested by the health department. He has cut down to a drink or two on three evenings in the two weeks and has not played cards. He feels low about being away from his practice but has no thoughts of suicide. [S]

list.item:
Cavitary pulmonary tuberculosis, intensive phase (A15.0). Early clinical response and full adherence. Baseline sputum cultures are growing Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex; susceptibility results are pending. ALT 41, AST 39, and bilirubin 0.7 at two weeks, all normal. Vision normal on ethambutol. HIV negative; hepatitis B and C serology negative, with no hepatitis B immunity. Infectious diseases agrees with the standard regimen and plan. [S]
Continue the four drugs and pyridoxine daily by video-observed therapy, taken at bedtime with a snack.
Three sputum samples on consecutive mornings in one week for the release decision.
Stop ethambutol once the isolate is shown to be susceptible to isoniazid and rifampin.
Liver tests monthly throughout treatment; stop the doses and call the same day for hepatitis symptoms.

Alcohol use disorder, mild (F10.10). Drinking already cut down. Safety reviewed: no thoughts of suicide. [S]
Goal agreed: no alcohol until treatment ends.
First session with a substance-use counselor by video next week.
Medication offered (acamprosate, which does not affect the liver); he prefers counseling first.
